events.title: Simón Bolívar is born in Caracas
events.description: The future liberator of much of South America was born into a wealthy Venezuelan family on this day. He later led military campaigns that helped free several nations from Spanish rule.
events.significance: Bolívar became one of the central figures of Latin American independence. Ecuador and Venezuela still mark his birthday with a holiday.

events.title: Alexandre Dumas is born
events.description: The French writer was born in Villers-Cotterêts. He grew up to write swashbuckling serials that thrilled readers across Europe.
events.significance: Dumas wrote The Three Musketeers and The Count of Monte Cristo. These are still among the most widely read adventure novels in the world.

events.title: Mormon pioneers enter the Salt Lake Valley
events.description: Led by Brigham Young, the first group of Latter-day Saint pioneers arrived in the Salt Lake Valley after a long overland trek. At the time the region belonged to Mexico.
events.significance: The arrival led to the founding of Salt Lake City. Utah still celebrates the anniversary each year as Pioneer Day.

events.title: Hiram Bingham reaches Machu Picchu
events.description: The American explorer, guided by local people, reached the Inca site high in the Peruvian Andes. He brought it to wide international attention.
events.significance: Machu Picchu became one of the world's best-known archaeological sites and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

events.title: Supreme Court rules against Nixon's claim of absolute executive privilege
events.description: In United States v. Nixon, the Supreme Court ruled that President Richard Nixon had to hand over the White House tape recordings subpoenaed in the Watergate investigation.
events.significance: The ruling confirmed that no president is above the law. Nixon resigned about two weeks later.
